purpose: Measure how much faster production runs the purge's verification work than the disposable rehearsal host, so a one_percent rehearsal's extrapolated verification time can be judged at production speed.
run_by: owner, by hand over SSH (owner-authorised; recorded here afterwards)
safety: The query reads no table and writes nothing: it generates its rows in memory. On production it ran in an ordinary read session; on the rehearsal host in a throwaway container removed afterwards.
query: SELECT count(*), md5(string_agg(md5(t::text), '' ORDER BY t.i)) FROM (SELECT i, i::float8 * 1.37 AS f, i % 97 AS k, repeat(md5(i::text), 6) AS pad FROM generate_series(1, 3000000) AS i) AS t;
why_this_query: purge_copy_verify renders each copied row as row text, hashes it with md5 and aggregates the hashes in key order; this query does the same CPU and sort work without touching data.

commands: sudo docker exec -it -u postgres edf-speedtest psql -X -d postgres

factor.definition: slowest production run / fastest rehearsal-host run
factor.applied_to: verify_seconds only, for receipts measured in the image above (scripts/operator/lib/v3_purge_rehearsal_receipt.py)
factor.not_applied_to: index build, VACUUM FREEZE and FK validation, which keep rehearsal-host time
